{
  "description": "A C++ multi-sensor fusion navigation system (GNSS/INS/Camera) using factor graph optimization (Ceres Solver). It normalizes heterogeneous sensor inputs (IMU, GNSS, Camera) into a unified time-aligned data structure and fuses them to produce high-precision position/attitude estimates. It is not a generic track fusion engine for EO detections but a specific visual-inertial-GNSS navigation stack.",
  "version": "unknown",
  "capabilities": [
    {
      "name": "Data Normalization (Sensor Time-Alignment)",
      "capability_id": "CAP.FUSION.NORMALIZE",
      "coverage": "partial",
      "evidence_status": "verified",
      "confidence": 0.8,
      "evidence_refs": [
        "include/data/navdataque.h@73c0f817",
        "test/NavdataQueue.cc@73c0f817"
      ],
      "notes": "The repository implements a DataQueue class that ingests GNSS, IMU, and Camera data streams. It uses a background thread to sort incoming heterogeneous data points by timestamp (TimeFirst logic) into a unified deque of BaseData pointers. This constitutes normalization for navigation purposes (time-syncing sensors), but does not normalize EO detections or generic track formats."
    },
    {
      "name": "Track Fusion (GNSS/INS/Camera State Estimation)",
      "capability_id": "CAP.FUSION.FUSE",
      "coverage": "partial",
      "evidence_status": "verified",
      "confidence": 0.7,
      "evidence_refs": [
        "README.md@73c0f817",
        "CMakeLists.txt@73c0f817"
      ],
      "notes": "The system fuses GNSS (PPP/RTK), IMU, and Camera (VIO) data to produce a single unified state estimate (position, velocity, attitude). It supports loose and tight coupling. This is 'fusion' in the navigation sense (state estimation), but it does not perform multi-target track association or fusion of independent detection tracks (e.g., from EO sensors) as typically defined in defense architectures."
    },
    {
      "name": "Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO)",
      "capability_id": null,

      ],
      "notes": "Core capability of the repo. Uses OpenCV and Ceres for feature tracking and pose estimation, fused with IMU."
    },
    {
